- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; apply a 1–3% downward correction in subsequent periods.
- If sentiment turns bearish (≤0.33) and news volume drops to 0, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast by 2–4% if sentiment change is negative and news is low.
- Mean reversion is strong in 3–5 day windows; if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–3%.
- If sentiment change is negative and forecast is high, model often fails to correct; apply a 1–2% downward bias if sentiment change is -0.5 or lower.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in the cycle; reduce forecast by 1–3% if true outcome is below 70% of 30-day average.
